rationale: PINS the CommonJS surface evidence forms on exports rows AND the file-local declaration guard. Markers: `exports = {...}` members -> `exports-object`; `module.exports = {...}` members -> `module-exports-object`; deep member writes -> `deep-member-assignment`. NEGATIVE (the guard): `helper` and `declaredName` are DECLARED IN THIS FILE and also written on module.exports — their rows must carry NO moduleExports marker (the claim exists only where no declaration answers the name; the name model resolves them honestly, and an emitted claim would be refuted by the arbiter, measured as 7 refuted rows and resolved 407->400 before this guard). `module.exports = function(){}` is a CJS default VALUE, not an ES default export: no defaultExportForm marker. NOTE the guard also suppresses an OBJECT-LITERAL METHOD name (`run`): this analyzer symbolizes object-literal method names, so the same test the arbiter applies (a project declaration answers the name) is knowable in the file — those rows are left unmarked and the name model resolves them. That narrows the moduleExports claim population (honest: an emitted claim would be refuted). A VALUE REBIND (`exports = outsideValue`) is NOT claimable: it replaces the surface value and does not create a property named after the value — the measured instance was require.js:908 `exports = factory`, the ONE refuted row of the final arm (form `exports-binding` was outside the arbiter's documented five-form set AND the claim itself was semantically false).
